summary.oneLiner: Surya Roshni navigated a volatile Q4FY26 marked by Middle East export disruptions and domestic raw material shortages, resulting in flat revenue and compressed margins, but management guides for a record FY27 driven by a strategic pivot to high-margin North American exports and capacity expansion. The key inflection is the shift from reliance on volatile domestic government tenders to secured, high-realization export orders which are expected to offset domestic margin compression from labor/fuel costs.

one-line thesis: Surya Roshni navigated a volatile Q4FY26 marked by Middle East export disruptions and domestic raw material shortages, resulting in flat revenue and compressed margins, but management guides for a record FY27 driven by a strategic pivot to high-margin North American exports and capacity expansion. The key inflection is the shift from reliance on volatile domestic government tenders to secured, high-realization export orders which are expected to offset domestic margin compression from labor/fuel costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹2,163 Cr (Q4, flat YoY), ₹7,540 Cr (FY26, +1% YoY). EBITDA: ₹170 Cr (Q4, 7.9% margin), ₹541 Cr (FY26, 7.2% margin). PAT: ₹98 Cr (Q4), ₹286 Cr (FY26). Order Book: ₹1,000+ Cr (Steel, strong export mix); ₹160 Cr (Lighting). Net Debt: Zero (Net Cash Surplus ₹337 Cr). One-offs/Distortions: Q4 impacted by ~12k ton export loss due to Middle East crisis; Full year impacted by SAP implementation glitches in Q1 and elevated input costs.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~24-25% for FY27 (Target ₹9,400-9,500 Cr). Margin: Steel EBITDA/ton guided at ~₹4,700 (down from Q4's ₹5,121 due to cost pressures); Consolidated EBITDA target ₹680-700 Cr. Order Inflow: Strong visibility from US exports (65k tons booked). Capex/Commissioning: Capacity to reach 1.6 Mn tons in FY27; 1.9 Mn tons by FY29.
order book & pipeline: Steel Division: ₹1,000+ Crores (led by exports, spiral, domestic API); Lighting Division: ₹160 Crores (Professional Lighting).
segment / subsidiary detail: Steel: Q4 Rev ₹1,662 Cr, Vol 2.6 Lakh tons (record), EBITDA/ton ₹5,121. FY26 Vol 9.04 Lakh tons (+3% YoY), Value-added mix 43%. Lighting: Q4 Rev ₹501 Cr (+9% YoY), EBITDA ₹44 Cr (8.8% margin). FY26 Rev ₹1,809 Cr (+7% YoY). Wire & Cable: FY26 Rev ₹38 Cr, FY27 Target ₹260 Cr.
growth verticals / optionality: North America export pivot (targeting 2.5 Lakh tons in FY27 vs 1.36 Lakh tons in FY26 with ₹9k-10k/ton EBITDA); Capacity expansion to 1.9 Mn tons by FY29; Wire & Cable scaling to ₹500-600 Cr run-rate; Potential demerger of Lighting business.
margins & cost dynamics: Pressure from new labor laws (₹30-40 Cr impact), rising fuel/power costs, and imported raw materials for Lighting (30-35% import content). Domestic API/tender margins compressed due to competition; offset by high-margin US exports.
capex / expansion: Focused on capacity addition: +2 Lakh tons in last 18 months; targeting 1.6 Mn tons in FY27 and 1.9 Mn tons in FY28-29. Funding via internal accruals (zero debt).
capital allocation: Strict 1/3 rule: 1/3 to dividends (₹5.00/share declared for FY26), 1/3 to business growth/working capital, 1/3 to capex. Considering share buyback as regulations ease.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability affecting exports; Delay in Indian government capex (Jal Jeevan/City Gas) impacting domestic volumes; Raw material (HR Coil) availability constraints; Execution risk on margin guidance given rising input costs.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic but defensive on past misses; Emphasizes 'conservative guidance' to avoid over-promising; Confident on FY27 being a 'record year' driven by exports; Transparent about labor/fuel headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly lowered FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance (₹4,700) despite higher export mix, citing massive hidden cost inflation (labor/fuel) that peers may not be fully pricing in; The 'Middle East crisis' blocked 12k tons in Q4 but simultaneously accelerated the strategic pivot to the US market which offers double the EBITDA/ton.

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.
themes.driver: Capex commissioning converting to volume; solar-structure & infra demand; commodity pass-through.
